title: decompose-init-values-and-add-configmap-rate-control-for-init-jobs
author: Liam O'Connor
commits: split values into values.init.yaml, values.seeding.yaml and retain values.core.yaml for runtime
introduce values.init.jobRateLimit and values.init.concurrentWorkers with sensible defaults
add go-templates helpers in templates/_init-helpers.tpl to compute tenant concurrency and bucket names
implement configmap-based leaky-bucket rate limiter template and unit tests
docs: add README-UPGRADE.md and migrate-init-values.sh helper
release_notes: Split init-related configuration into a dedicated values file and add a simple configmap leaky-bucket rate limiter with per-tenant concurrency annotations; include migration steps for existing private installs.
description: Background and motivation: upgrades and mass tenant onboarding in on-prem clusters sometimes trigger many concurrent init jobs (seed/migrate/validate) which created API throttling and scheduling pressure. This PR separates init-specific settings into values.init.yaml so operators can tune init behavior independently, and introduces a configmap-based leaky-bucket rate control with an annotation-driven per-tenant concurrency cap. Changes made: values.init.yaml added with fields jobRateLimit, concurrentWorkers, retryPolicy and bucketConfig; values.schema.json extended with validation blocks for the init group; templates/_init-helpers.tpl contains functions renderInitConcurrency and rateLimitBucketName used by init job templates; templates/init/rate-limiter-configmap.yaml creates a cluster-scoped limiter that init jobs consult via annotations; templates/init/jobs-seed.yaml updated to use the helpers and to annotate jobs with tenant id and desired concurrency; tests added for helm template rendering and values schema validation; README-UPGRADE.md includes a recommended migration workflow and a migrate-init-values.sh helper for operators. CI and testing: local unit tests for template helpers, linting, values schema CI job, and a staged e2e run on a 3-AZ cluster with ~50 tenants in staging to validate throttling behavior. Rollback and safety: init orchestration writes a status configmap with TTL; chart hooks are guarded to avoid double-apply during rollback and the limiter includes fallbacks to cluster defaults when tenant annotations are absent. Operational notes: operators should copy init keys from existing values.yaml into values.init.yaml using the migration helper, set init.jobRateLimit conservatively (default recommended 5), and optionally tune per-tenant concurrency via annotation redwood.io/init-concurrency. This implementation intentionally avoids introducing a new controller at this stage; follow-up work will consider a controller-based quota manager for richer accounting. Related tickets: ENG-4021, ENG-4199 and SUP-731.
note_to_ops: See charts/private-installer/README-UPGRADE.md for step-by-step migration. Run scripts/migrate-init-values.sh to split values; apply the chart with a conservative init.jobRateLimit (2-5) before scaling up tenants; use annotation redwood.io/init-concurrency to cap per-tenant workers. If you encounter persistent rate errors after upgrading, set init.jobRateLimit to lower value and inspect the rate-limiter configmap and init-status configmaps for TTL entries. The chart includes tests/values-validation-test.yaml to help validate operator-provided values before deployment.
